Psoriasis – What You Should Know
Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated skin condition that causes red, scaly, itchy plaques, most commonly over the scalp, elbows, knees, and lower back. It is not contagious.
Why does it occur?
Overactive immune response
Genetic predisposition
Triggers such as stress, infections, skin injury, and certain medications
Common symptoms
Thick, silvery scales
Redness and itching
Dry, cracked skin
Nail changes and joint pain in some patients
Management & Treatment
Psoriasis is controllable with the right care:
Topical treatments (medicated creams and lotions)
Phototherapy
Oral medications and biologics for moderate to severe cases give excewlner clearnace and improve quality of life
Lifestyle modifications and regular follow-up
Early diagnosis and individualized treatment can significantly improve skin health and quality of life.
Consult a dermatologist for long-term control and flare prevention.

Acne is a common skin condition that occurs when oil glands become overactive and pores get blocked with oil, dead skin cells, and bacteria. It commonly affects the face, chest, and back, especially during adolescence, but can occur at any age.

Common Causes

Oily skin

Hormonal changes (teenage years, menstrual cycles, PCOS)

Stress

Genetics

Certain cosmetics and medications


Acne Treatment Options

Treatment depends on the severity of acne and skin type:

Topical treatments: Medicated creams and gels to reduce oil, bacteria, and inflammation

Oral medications: Antibiotics or isotretinoin for moderate to severe acne

Procedural treatments: Chemical peels, light-based therapies, and medical facials


Treatment for Acne Marks & Scars

Chemical peels

Microneedling / Dermaroller

MNRF (Microneedling Radiofrequency)

Laser treatments


👉 Early treatment helps prevent scarring. Always consult a dermatologist for a personalized plan
